key_insight: LatentRL-QAS enables transfer across qubit counts by reusing learned circuit representations in a shared latent space while keeping the RL agent’s dimensions fixed.
engineering_relevance: Decoupling the RL agent from qubit count removes the need to enlarge its state, action space, and network when searching larger quantum circuits.
method: Encode circuits as one token per gate using a variational autoencoder with a shared latent space.
Train an RL agent to navigate latent representations rather than add gates directly.
Periodically refresh the representation with new discoveries and expand it for larger systems using smaller-system solutions.
evidence_signal: On five- and six-qubit absolutely maximally entangled state tasks, LatentRL-QAS succeeded in 89–99% of evaluation episodes; baseline RL-QAS found neither target under the same budget despite 10–17× larger networks.
watch_item: Transfer is demonstrated on AME-state preparation; its effectiveness and representation-refresh costs for broader circuit-design tasks remain to be established.
paper_title: LatentRL-QAS: Transfer via Latent Reinforcement Learning for Quantum Architecture Search
